text: score = 0.6 × the protocol node's own rating + 0.4 × the TVL-weighted mean (weight = tvl_30d_ma share) of the latest published score of every rated vault that deposits into it; with no rated vault the node rating stands alone (applied.k1 = 1). The band is read straight off the thresholds, without the dwell rule that smooths vault bands, so it can move on any day. A vault that deposits into more than one protocol node (every Morpho vault: the framework and the Blue instance) counts toward each. Vault scores are the published ones — their caps were computed against the node rating as of their own date, so after a node re-rate the two terms agree again at the next nightly. chain_id narrows the vault set only.

risklayer.summary: Morpho is a modular lending protocol with ~$6.5B TVL across 37+ EVM chains, built around immutable Morpho Blue core markets and curator-managed vaults. The lending logic itself has never been directly exploited and carries tier-1 audit coverage plus Certora formal verification, but governance is concentrated in a 5-of-9 multisig with no protocol-wide timelock, permissionless oracle selection has produced recurring market-level losses (~$480K in Oct 2024), and seven cross-chain deployments lack block-explorer verification. Overall risk is moderate (4.8/10).

details.name: Dependency Risk
details.description: Permissionless oracle selection with Chainlink feeds lacking staleness checks, no fallback oracles, and a paused LayerZero MORPHO bridge with multisig-controlled setPeer.

details.name: Governance Risk
details.description: 5/9 Gnosis Safe execution with no protocol-wide timelock, off-chain Snapshot voting without on-chain enforcement, and multisig control over token upgrades and LayerZero bridge configuration.

details.name: Tokenomics Risk
details.description: Fixed 1B supply with ~88% allocated to treasury, investors, and insiders; significant vesting unlocks through 2028, no fee-switch value capture, and discretionary DAO reward emissions.

details.name: Audit Coverage Risk
details.description: Industry-leading multi-firm audit program with Certora formal verification on core contracts; residual gaps are unverified cross-chain bytecode, one risk-accepted Vault V2 finding, and off-chain SDK/frontend outside audit scope.

details.name: Smart Contract Risk
details.description: Morpho Blue core is immutable and extensively audited, but seven cross-chain deployments lack block-explorer verification, the MORPHO token uses UUPS upgradeable proxies, and permissionless market creation creates oracle misconfiguration exposure.

risklayer.note: Risklayer is in beta and publishes no ordering for its bands, so the figure is shown exactly as reported.

findings.title: Unverified Morpho Blue on Base
findings.description: Morpho Blue at 0xBBBBBbbBBb9cC5e90e3b3Af64bdAF62C37EEFFCb on Base is marked unverified in pipeline discovery. On-chain bytecode length (15,623 bytes) matches Ethereum deployment; owner() resolves to 5/9 governance Safe 0xcBa28b38103307Ec8dA98377ffF9816C164f9AFa. Source cannot be independently confirmed on Base explorer despite verified Ethereum sibling — blocks chain-specific audit assurance.

findings.title: Unverified Morpho ChainlinkOracleV2 Factory on Arbitrum
findings.description: Oracle factory 0x3585E3fD72F8d1b02250E1F6496b706c6e092884 on Arbitrum has no deployed bytecode (eth_getCode returns empty). Listed in discovery but cannot be source-audited; if used for oracle deployment, misconfiguration risk is unmitigated by verification.

findings.title: Unverified MetaMorpho Factory Alt on Ethereum
findings.description: MetaMorpho Factory V1.1 alt at 0x83A7f60c9fc57cEf1e8001bda98783AA1A53E4b1 on Ethereum has no deployed bytecode. Address appears in discovery but is a ghost entry with no auditable source.

findings.title: Unverified VaultV2Factory on Arbitrum
findings.description: VaultV2Factory at 0x6b46fa3cc9EBF8aB230aBAc664E37F2966Bf7971 on Arbitrum is unverified per pipeline status. Bytecode is identical to verified Ethereum VaultV2Factory (23,124 bytes), but absence of Arbiscan verification prevents independent source confirmation for the ~$6.5B TVL vault stack.

findings.title: Unverified Bundler3 on Base
findings.description: Bundler3 periphery at 0x6BFd8137e702540E7A42B74178A4a49Ba43920C4 on Base is unverified. Bytecode matches verified Ethereum Bundler3 exactly (1,547 bytes). Users interacting via Morpho App rely on unverified bytecode; April 2025 frontend incident routed approvals to Bundler3.

findings.title: Unverified MORPHO LayerZero OFT on Arbitrum
findings.description: MORPHO OFT at 0x40BD670A58238e6E230c430BBb5cE6ec0d40df48 on Arbitrum is unverified (855 bytes deployed). Standard owner() reverts; ERC-1967 implementation slot references Ethereum MorphoOFTAdapter. Cross-chain bridge was proactively suspended following LayerZero infrastructure incident (Apr 2026). Unverified bridge token contract is a critical visibility gap.

findings.title: Unverified Governance Multisig on Base
findings.description: Morpho governance Gnosis Safe at 0xcBa28b38103307Ec8dA98377ffF9816C164f9AFa on Base is unverified per pipeline status. On-chain it is a standard GnosisSafeProxy (171 bytes) with identical bytecode to verified Ethereum deployment; getThreshold()=5, getOwners()=9 signers. Unverified status blocks independent confirmation of proxy singleton configuration on Base.

findings.title: No Timelock on Governance Multisig Execution
findings.description: The primary 5/9 Gnosis Safe can execute privileged actions immediately once threshold signatures are collected. There is no on-chain TimelockController or Safe module enforcing a delay between vote passage and execution. This applies to Morpho Blue owner functions (enableIrm, enableLltv, setFee, setFeeRecipient), MORPHO token upgrades, LayerZero bridge configuration, and MorphoRegistry updates.

findings.title: Upgradeable MORPHO Token Controlled by Governance Multisig
findings.description: The MORPHO token on Ethereum (0x58D97B57BB95320F9a05dC918Aef65434969c2B2) is an ERC1967 upgradeable proxy. owner() resolves to the governance multisig, granting the ability to upgrade token logic without a timelock. Base MORPHO (0xBAa5CC21fd487B8Fcc2F632f3F4E8D37262a0842) shares the same owner.

findings.title: Permissionless Oracle Selection With No Protocol-Level Safeguards
findings.description: Morpho Blue accepts any IOracle at market creation. The core contract explicitly states it is the user's responsibility to select safe oracles. Misconfigured oracles caused ~$480K in isolated market exploits (Oct 2024 PAXG/USDC SCALE_FACTOR and LeadBlock incidents). This is a systemic dependency risk across all markets, not a core contract bug.

findings.title: June 2023 AaveV3-ETH Optimizer Index Caching Vulnerability
findings.description: Researcher GothicShanon89238 disclosed via Immunefi a flash-loan index-inflation bug in legacy Morpho Optimizer (not Morpho Blue). Attack required ~$101M capital over 2+ blocks and could have drained user funds. Supply was paused within hours; fix merged Jun 8 and re-reviewed by Spearbit and Runtime Verification. No funds lost; $285,000 bounty paid.

findings.title: October 2024 LeadBlock PAXG/USDC Oracle Misconfiguration
findings.description: Attacker deposited ~$350 PAXG and borrowed ~$230K USDC after LeadBlock misconfigured oracle SCALE_FACTOR (12-decimal error between PAXG 18-dec and USDC 6-dec), inflating gold price to ~$2.6T. DeFiLlama lists this as 'LeadBlock's Morpho Blue Market' at $250K (Oct 14). Isolated to a permissionless user-deployed market; Morpho core contracts unaffected.
